title: Mirage Archer Guide — Dodge Trigger, Socketed Attacks, Cooldown and Limits
summary: Mirage Archer is a Meta gem that, when you Dodge Roll, spawns a Mirage that uses the attacks socketed into it. The Mirage mimics your ranged attacks (Bow / Spear / Crossbow) with a damage penalty, has its own object limit separate from yours, and cannot use supports that say 'Skills you use yourself'. This guide explains the dodge trigger, cooldown, multiple Mirages, socketed-attack priority, the Lightning Rod / Lightning Arrow interaction, and the mapping / bossing rotations used by Deadeye, Witchhunter and Gemling builds.
description: Mirage Archer deep guide: dodge-roll trigger and Mirage creation, 60 Spirit cost, duration and cooldown, single vs multiple socketed attacks and priority, object limits independent of the player, Uses / Reload / Channelling behaviour, Lightning Rod and Lightning Arrow interaction, supports that say 'yourself', Spirit budget vs Herald / Combat Frenzy, mapping and bossing rotations, troubleshooting and community evidence.
author: Exile2 Guides Editorial

sections.title: Quick Answer: Dodge Roll Spawns a Mirage
paragraphs: Mirage Archer does not fire anything itself. When you Dodge Roll, it spawns a Mirage that uses the attacks you have socketed into the gem, at a damage penalty.
The Mirage effectively doubles your ranged output for its duration — as long as the socketed skills are valid ranged attacks and the cooldown is ready.

sections.title: Requirements and Setup
paragraphs: Mirage Archer needs a Bow, Spear or Crossbow equipped and at least one valid ranged attack socketed into the gem. The Mirage can only use skills that are themselves ranged attacks — melee and unsupported skills are ignored.
Because it is a Meta gem, you socket it alongside the attacks you want mimicked; the gem itself is the trigger, not the damage source.

keyValues.label: Weapon
notes: Melee skills are not mimicked.

keyValues.label: Socketed skill
notes: Only valid ranged attacks are used by the Mirage.

sections.title: Mirage Creation and Limits
paragraphs: The Mirage is created on Dodge Roll and lasts a short duration before expiring. On the current client the cooldown begins when the Mirage is created, so you cannot spawn a new one until the previous is consumed or its duration ends — confirm the exact cooldown on client 0.5.4.
Multiple Mirages cannot normally coexist; one dodge produces one Mirage, and the next dodge is gated by the cooldown. The Mirage's object count is tracked separately from your own deployed objects.

sections.title: Socketed Attacks and Priority
paragraphs: You can socket a single attack or several. With multiple socketed attacks, the Mirage uses them according to a priority / rotation rather than all at once. Skills with built-in Uses, Grenades or Ammunition behave specially — the Mirage may need to reload or may not fire if it lacks the initial Uses.
A common mismatch is Freezing Salvo: it can be socketed, but the Mirage may not fire if it does not have the initial Uses available, so it looks like 'nothing happened'.

notes: Simplest, most predictable setup.

keyValues.label: Multiple skills
notes: Mirage picks per its internal priority.

keyValues.label: Uses / Grenade / Ammo
notes: May need reload or lack initial Uses (e.g. Freezing Salvo).

sections.title: Object Limits Independent of Player
paragraphs: The Mirage's deployed objects (such as Lightning Rods it places) are counted against the Mirage's own limit, separate from your player limit. That means you and the Mirage can each have your own set of rods up to the respective caps.

This independence is also where the known Lightning Rod + Lightning Arrow bug appears: the Mirage's rods and your rods can interact in unexpected ways, so test the combo on the current client before relying on it.

keyValues.label: Mirage limit
notes: Each tracks its own deployed-object cap.

keyValues.label: Interaction bug
notes: Known issue; verify behaviour on client 0.5.4.

sections.title: Mechanics: Uses, Reload and Cooldown
paragraphs: The Mirage inherits the socketed attack's mechanics, including Uses and Reload. An attack that reloads will make the Mirage reload too, which is why Explosive Shot's clip behaviour shows up on the Mirage as well.
The Mirage's lifespan is short, so skills that need a long wind-up or many Uses may not finish before it expires. Pick socketed attacks that pay off quickly.

sections.title: Skill Interactions
paragraphs: Explosive Shot works through the Mirage but keeps its clip/reload behaviour. Lightning Arrow is a clean mimic with no reload. Lightning Rod is limited and has the known player-Arrow bug, so the Lightning Rod + Lightning Arrow pair needs testing on the Mirage.
Snipe is supported from 0.5 onward as a channeled attack; the Mirage channels it but timing on release matters.

sections.title: Support Compatibility
paragraphs: Duration supports extend the Mirage's life, which is the main lever for getting more attacks out of it. Cooldown supports shorten the dodge-to-dodge gap. Avoid supports that explicitly say 'Skills you use yourself' — the Mirage is not you, so those do not apply to its attacks.

keyValues.label: Duration supports
notes: Longer Mirage = more mimicked attacks.

keyValues.label: Cooldown supports
notes: Shorten the dodge gap.

keyValues.label: 'Skills you use yourself'
notes: The Mirage is not the player.

sections.title: Spirit Budget Trade-offs
paragraphs: At 60 Spirit, Mirage Archer is expensive and competes with Herald buffs and Combat Frenzy for the same pool. On a ranged build you must decide whether the mimicked damage is worth more than an aura or charge generator.
Most Deadeye and Witchhunter ranged builds keep it because the doubled ranged output is large, but tight-Spirit builds may drop it.

keyValues.label: Cost
notes: Same pool as Herald / Combat Frenzy.

keyValues.label: Trade-off
notes: Drop only if Spirit is the bottleneck.

sections.title: Where It Is Used
paragraphs: Deadeye and Witchhunter ranged builds use Mirage Archer to double their bow / crossbow output. Gemling Legionnaire variants use it when they can afford the 60 Spirit and want the mimicked damage.
In every case the build values the doubled ranged attack more than the lost Spirit aura.

sections.title: Community Evidence
paragraphs: Community reports cluster on the Lightning Rod bug (Mirage rods interacting with the player's Arrow) and on skill selection (why Freezing Salvo 'does nothing'). Client testing confirms the Mirage uses a priority over socketed ranged attacks and that Uses / reload skills behave specially.
The 'yourself' support misconception is common: supports that say Skills you use yourself do not apply to the Mirage's attacks.
